title: Partial Identification of Boundary Effects from Rounded Distance without Location or Angle
banked_reason: Cold general review: publishability_tier=subfield, meets_floor=false, paper_score_ceiling=7.2; exact per-Q endpoints and attainability remain open.
gap_reasons: The exact release-law-specific endpoint characterization remains open.
Without endpoint attainability or a sharp diameter constant, the honestly positioned PartialID contribution is subfield rather than field tier (paper-score ceiling 7.2).
The Cattaneo–Titiunik–Yu exact-distance class does not contain this rounded-release experiment, so its results cannot supply the missing lift.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the release-fiber diameter bounds 2 c_L Δ ≤ ω_Δ ≤ 4 L Δ, a computable certified outer interval, the joint sampling/alias minimax frontier, and matching honest expected-length results; the math and decision reviews pass, and the Hoeffding leaf is cited, verified, and attested. The field-tier attempt collapsed only on novelty: exact per-Q endpoints, endpoint attainability, and the sharp maximal-diameter constant remain unproved and require new mathematics.
tldr: An analyst observes only \(Z_\Delta=(Y,T,Q_\Delta(R))\): bounded outcome, sharp-treatment side, and floor-rounded distance from one fixed boundary point; raw location, polar angle, and raw radius are unavailable. For each attainable released law \(Q\), its first-bin side means \(\eta_t(Q)=\mathbb E_Q[Y\mid T=t,Q_\Delta(R)=0]\) give clipped anchor intervals \([\underline{\theta}_t(Q),\overline{\theta}_t(Q)]\), where \(\underline{\theta}_t(Q)=\max\{0,\eta_t(Q)-L\Delta\}\) and \(\overline{\theta}_t(Q)=\min\{1,\eta_t(Q)+L\Delta\}\). Thus \(I_\Delta(Q)\) is contained in the directly computable certified outer interval \([\underline{\theta}_1(Q)-\overline{\theta}_0(Q),\overline{\theta}_1(Q)-\underline{\theta}_0(Q)]\); equality and exact sharp endpoints are not claimed. The maximal release-fiber diameter satisfies \(2c_L\Delta\leq\omega_\Delta\leq4L\Delta\). Supporting statistical frontiers give absolute-risk and honest-expected-length order \(\max\{n^{-1/4},\Delta\}\), with squared risk of the corresponding squared order.
gap: Exact-coordinate boundary methods do not describe the identified set after angle and within-bin radius are removed. Scalar measurement-error methods require auxiliary discrepancy information to restore identification, and manipulation-based partial-identification methods address latent assignment types rather than a known deterministic release map; neither evaluates the release fiber of a fixed bivariate point-boundary effect.
fill: The paper fixes the analyst's observation \(\sigma\)-field, defines the release-fiber identified set \(I_\Delta(Q)\), and bounds its worst diameter between \(2c_L\Delta\) and \(4L\Delta\). Matching minimax-risk and honest-length frontiers then separate this population ambiguity from the additional \(n^{-1/4}\) sampling cost.
